dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For each natural number n, this is the type of admissible n-dimensional run packages generated by D006. A package contains a positive dimension, a matrix norm, positive epsilon, a nonnegative function mu, seven real n-by-n matrices, two nonnegative inherited-error bounds, an exact decomposition of the computed product, and three norm bounds.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target universally quantifies over every inhabitant of this package type, so all data and conditions stored in a run act as the universally quantified data and hypotheses of the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a run, this proposition is the conjunction of (1) residual(run) = localFirstOrderError + (exactLeft * rightPerturbation + leftPerturbation * exactRight), and (2) N(exactLeft * rightPerturbation) <= N(exactLeft) * rightInheritedError.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is exactly the conclusion asserted for every admissible run.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the value function of a packaged matrix norm: given a norm package N and a matrix A, it returns the real number N(A).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets every occurrence of matrixNorm.value as evaluation of the chosen matrix norm.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the localFirstOrderError matrix, the twelfth field of a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the matrix E appearing as the first term on the right side of the residual identity.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the matrix-norm package, the second field of a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the norm N used in the asserted inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructs a run from n with 0 < n; a matrix norm N; epsilon > 0; a function mu : Nat -> Real with mu(k) >= 0 for every k; matrices X, Y, dX, dY, C, E, and H; nonnegative real bounds a and b; the identity C = ((X + dX)(Y + dY) + E) + H; and bounds N(E) <= mu(n) epsilon N(X) N(Y), N(dX) <= a, and N(dY) <= b.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the complete data and hypotheses encoded by an admissible run and hence the assumptions under which the two conclusions must hold.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: For n, this is the type of real n-by-n matrices, represented as Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All seven matrix-valued fields and every matrix expression in the proposition have this type.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a run, this is the left-associated residual ((C - X*Y) - dX*dY) - H, where C is the computed product, X and Y are the exact factors, dX and dY are their perturbations, and H is the higher-order remainder.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the entire left side of the asserted matrix equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a run, this is the matrix product dX*Y of the left perturbation and the exact right factor.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the second cross term in the residual equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a run, this is the matrix product X*dY of the exact left factor and the right perturbation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the first cross term in the residual equality and the matrix whose norm is bounded in the second conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a run, this is the real number N(X) * b, where b is rightInheritedError.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the right side of the asserted norm inequality N(X*dY) <= N(X)b.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: For each n, this is the type of matrix-norm packages generated by D021: a real-valued function on real n-by-n matrices satisfying nonnegativity, definiteness, absolute homogeneity, the triangle inequality, and submultiplicativity.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It restricts the run's norm to an arbitrary norm with the listed axioms, including the submultiplicativity needed to relate N(X*dY) to N(X)N(dY).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the computedProduct matrix C, the eleventh field of a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies C in the residual on the left side of the matrix equality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the exactLeft matrix X, the seventh field of a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies X in the exact product, a cross product, and the norm bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the exactRight matrix Y, the eighth field of a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies Y in the exact product and the left-perturbation cross product.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the higherOrderRemainder matrix H, the thirteenth field of a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is subtracted in the residual and is also part of the run's exact decomposition hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the leftPerturbation matrix dX, the ninth field of a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies dX in the perturbation product dX*dY and the cross product dX*Y.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef018
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the real rightInheritedError bound b, the fifteenth field of a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the factor multiplying N(X) on the right side of the second conclusion and is assumed to bound N(dY).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef019
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the rightPerturbation matrix dY, the tenth field of a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies dY in dX*dY, X*dY, and the asserted norm inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef020
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is ordinary multiplication of two real n-by-n matrices.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the meaning of X*Y, dX*dY, X*dY, dX*Y, and the expanded product in the run hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef021
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructs a matrix norm N from a function N : M_n -> Real satisfying N(A) >= 0; N(A) = 0 iff A = 0; N(cA) = |c|N(A); N(A+B) <= N(A)+N(B); and N(AB) <= N(A)N(B), for all appropriate real scalars and matrices.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It precisely specifies what properties the arbitrary matrix norm stored in a run possesses.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the domain of the universally quantified dimension n and of the function mu.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: This forms the logical conjunction of two propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires both the residual equality and the norm inequality to hold.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is equality between two terms of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses the matrix equality in the conclusion and equalities appearing in the run and norm axioms.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite type of indices from 0 through n-1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It indexes the rows and columns of every n-by-n matrix.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the available heterogeneous addition operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Here it denotes ordinary matrix addition in matrix expressions and ordinary real addition in scalar norm axioms.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the available less-than-or-equal relation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Here it denotes the standard real order in all nonnegativity and norm-bound conditions.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.add
dependency_coverage.meaning: This defines matrix addition pointwise from addition of entries.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All sums of matrices in the run hypothesis and residual equality are pointwise matrix sums.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Matrix entries, norm values, epsilon, values of mu, and inherited-error bounds are all real.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is ordinary addition on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the scalar addition used by the norm axioms and the underlying real arithmetic.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the standard less-than-or-equal order on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets all displayed inequalities as ordinary real inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This turns an ordinary addition operation on a type into homogeneous heterogeneous addition on that same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes each hAdd occurrence ordinary matrix or real addition, according to its operands.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the available heterogeneous multiplication operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Here it denotes ordinary multiplication of real norm values and bounds; matrix multiplication is supplied through the specialized matrix instance used by D020.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the available heterogeneous subtraction operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the three left-associated matrix subtractions in the residual.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the available strict-order relation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses the assumptions 0 < n and 0 < epsilon.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix
dependency_coverage.meaning: A matrix with row type m, column type n, and entries in alpha is a function m -> n -> alpha.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes each real n-by-n matrix a doubly indexed function on Fin n.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.sub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This defines matrix subtraction pointwise from subtraction of entries.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Each subtraction in the residual is ordinary pointwise subtraction of real matrices.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets a natural-number literal in a type having the corresponding numeral instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the literal 0 in positivity, nonnegativity, definiteness, and zero-matrix statements.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the standard strict order on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets 0 < epsilon as ordinary strict positivity of epsilon.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is ordinary multiplication on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets products such as mu(n) epsilon N(X) N(Y) and N(X)b as ordinary real products.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is ordinary real subtraction, defined as addition of the additive inverse.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Through pointwise matrix subtraction, it gives the entrywise meaning of the residual's subtractions.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the real number zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies zero in real positivity, nonnegativity, and norm-definiteness conditions.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: This converts a type's zero element into its interpretation of the numeral 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures that real and matrix occurrences of the literal 0 denote their respective zero elements.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This turns ordinary multiplication on a type into homogeneous heterogeneous multiplication on that type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes scalar hMul expressions ordinary multiplication of real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: instHSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This turns ordinary subtraction on a type into homogeneous heterogeneous subtraction on that type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the hSub operations in the residual ordinary matrix subtraction.

dependency_coverage.name: instLTNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the standard strict order on natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets 0 < n as strict positivity of the matrix dimension.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets each natural-number numeral as that natural number itself.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the natural number 0 in the condition 0 < n.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: This provides the finite enumeration of Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the inner-index sum in n-by-n matrix multiplication finite.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This defines matrix multiplication by (MN)(i,k) = sum over j of M(i,j)N(j,k), using the finite middle index type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It confirms that every matrix product in the proposition is standard finite-sum matrix multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This provides the commutative additive-monoid structure of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the finite sums used in real matrix multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: Algebra.id
dependency_coverage.meaning: This gives a commutative semiring its identity algebra structure over itself.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For the reals, it underlies real scalar multiplication of real matrices in the absolute-homogeneity norm axiom.

dependency_coverage.name: Algebra.toSMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the scalar-multiplication operation supplied by an algebra structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies multiplication of a real matrix by a real scalar in the norm homogeneity condition.

dependency_coverage.name: CommSemiring.toSemiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the underlying semiring structure from a commutative semiring.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the identity real algebra structure used for scalar multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: HSMul.hSMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the available heterogeneous scalar-multiplication operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It denotes the scalar multiple cA occurring in the absolute-homogeneity axiom for the matrix norm.

dependency_coverage.name: Iff
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is logical equivalence between two propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses norm definiteness as N(A) = 0 if and only if A is the zero matrix.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.smul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This defines scalar multiplication of a matrix pointwise from scalar multiplication of its entries.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The matrix cA in the norm homogeneity axiom is obtained by multiplying every entry of A by c.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.zero
dependency_coverage.meaning: This defines the zero matrix pointwise from the zero entry.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the meaning of A = 0 in the matrix norm's definiteness axiom.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: This provides the additive-group structure of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies additive inverses used in real absolute value and subtraction.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instCommSemiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: This provides the commutative-semiring operations and laws on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the identity real algebra, scalar multiplication, and real matrix multiplication used by the norm axioms.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice
dependency_coverage.meaning: This provides the lattice order structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the definition of the absolute value appearing in norm homogeneity.

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real number c, this is its absolute value, defined as max(c,-c).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It appears in the norm axiom N(cA) = |c|N(A).

dependency_coverage.name: instHSMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This turns an ordinary scalar action into heterogeneous scalar multiplication with the same result type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes hSMul c A the ordinary pointwise real scalar multiple of the matrix A.

binders: A universally quantified natural number n.

An arbitrary admissible run at dimension n, equivalently data consisting of a matrix norm N on real n-by-n matrices; a real epsilon; a function mu : Nat -> Real; matrices X, Y, dX, dY, C, E, H in M_n; and real inherited-error bounds a and b.
hypotheses: N is nonnegative, definite, absolutely homogeneous, subadditive, and submultiplicative: N(A) >= 0; N(A) = 0 iff A = 0; N(cA) = |c|N(A); N(A+B) <= N(A)+N(B); and N(AB) <= N(A)N(B).
mu is pointwise nonnegative: mu(k) >= 0 for every natural number k.
The inherited-error bounds are nonnegative: 0 <= a and 0 <= b.
The computed product has the exact decomposition C = ((X+dX)(Y+dY)+E)+H.
The local first-order error satisfies N(E) <= mu(n) epsilon N(X) N(Y).
The perturbations satisfy N(dX) <= a and N(dY) <= b.
conclusions: The left-associated residual satisfies ((C - X*Y) - dX*dY) - H = E + (X*dY + dX*Y).
The exact-left/right-perturbation cross term satisfies N(X*dY) <= N(X)b.
mathematical_definitions: M_n is the space of real n-by-n matrices indexed by Fin n in both coordinates.
Matrix addition, subtraction, zero, and real scalar multiplication are pointwise.
Matrix multiplication is standard multiplication: (AB)(i,k) = sum over j in Fin n of A(i,j)B(j,k).

X = exactLeft, Y = exactRight, dX = leftPerturbation, dY = rightPerturbation, C = computedProduct, E = localFirstOrderError, H = higherOrderRemainder, a = leftInheritedError, and b = rightInheritedError.
The residual in the first conclusion is defined with exact left association as ((C - X*Y) - dX*dY) - H.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural dimension n and every admissible run with n > 0, let X and Y be exact real n-by-n matrices, dX and dY their perturbations, C the computed product, E a local first-order error, H a higher-order remainder, N an arbitrary submultiplicative matrix norm, and b a nonnegative bound satisfying N(dY) <= b. If C is exactly ((X+dX)(Y+dY)+E)+H, together with the other packaged positivity and error-bound assumptions, then subtracting X*Y, dX*dY, and H successively from C leaves exactly E + X*dY + dX*Y, with the stated parenthesization E + (X*dY + dX*Y). Moreover, the norm of X*dY is at most N(X)b.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem quantifies over packaged admissible runs; it does not assert that such a run exists for any n or for any chosen data.
Because every run contains a proof of 0 < n, the assertion for n = 0 is vacuous.
The matrix norm is arbitrary subject only to the five supplied norm axioms; no particular induced or entrywise norm is selected.
epsilon is required only to be positive; no smallness condition such as epsilon < 1 is encoded.
mu is arbitrary and pointwise nonnegative. Its value mu(n) appears only in a hypothesis constraining E and not in either conclusion.
The local-error bound, the left inherited-error bound, and positivity of several packaged scalars are assumptions on admissible runs but do not appear directly in the two conclusions.
The second conclusion bounds only the cross term X*dY. It does not provide a bound for dX*Y, dX*dY, the complete residual, or the total computed-product error.
All arithmetic is exact arithmetic over real matrices. No floating-point operation, rounding mode, computational algorithm, or probabilistic model is encoded.
There are no existential quantifiers or existential witnesses in the target.
